approach: Add a SnapshotRepo::PlainWithHistory variant. Snapshot::create handles it like None (plain files, no .git), then writes HISTORY.txt in the snapshot root. The file comes from one `git log` run on the user's repo at source_commit, read-only. Paths are filtered with the existing `classify` (records/ and athena-exclude dropped). It keeps the newest 200 commits that still have a visible path or had no paths at all. The planner and critic snapshots in run.rs switch to the new variant. The reader stays on None. The inline planner/critic grant becomes a named function with an unchanged value, so a test can pin it. Both briefs get one shared paragraph, built from the HISTORY_FILE constant and a HISTORY_LIMIT constant, saying what the file holds and that Read and Grep are the tools for it. CHANGELOG and decisions.md record the choice and a measured time.

decisions.choice: Generate a text file from `git log` in the user's repo; put no repository in the snapshot.
decisions.reason: Gives the history facts (shape of real PR ranges) with grants unchanged and no .git, so nothing can write or reach hidden history.

rejected.option: Put a git repository with history in the snapshot
rejected.why: Excluded by the request. It would need a history rewrite to hide records/ and private paths, and it opens git commands.

rejected.option: Widen the planner and critic grants to git log/show/diff
rejected.why: Out of scope; the user dropped it. It also exposes records/ and private paths to the agents.
It leaves out the facts only history shows, which caused the stops and rejections.

decisions.choice: The reader's SnapshotRepo::None stays; a new variant PlainWithHistory is used for the planner and critic only.
decisions.reason: The reader, producer and verifier snapshots are out of scope and stay byte-identical. One enum match in `create` holds the logic.

rejected.option: A separate write_history call in run.rs after create
rejected.why: It duplicates the rules-commit filter at two call sites and is easy to miss, as the two sites already show.

decisions.choice: Filter with `classify(user, rules_commit, paths)` on all paths of the scanned commits in one batch. Omit a commit whose paths are all hidden. List a commit with no paths at all (an empty commit) as '(no paths)'. Scan at most 2000 commits before the 200 cap.
decisions.reason: Same filter as the file copy. The 200 are counted after exclusion. The scan cap bounds time on huge histories. A records-only commit says nothing about the code.

rejected.option: List hidden-only commits with no paths
rejected.why: It reveals that hidden work happened and spends the 200 slots.

decisions.choice: Format: one block per commit, `<short hash> <YYYY-MM-DD> <subject>` then indented path lines. Use `git log --first-parent -m --name-only --no-renames --format=...`.
decisions.reason: Easy for Read and Grep. It also gives paths for squash and merge commits, the shape of PR ranges.

files.purpose: Add SnapshotRepo::PlainWithHistory, HISTORY_FILE and HISTORY_LIMIT constants, the history writer, and tests (filter, cap, no .git, user repo unchanged).
Add a Git helper that runs the bounded `git log` and returns parsed commits (hash, date, subject, paths). Update the module doc if it mentions plain copies.
Use PlainWithHistory for the planner and critic snapshots. Extract the grant into `planning_grant()` and add the unchanged-grant test.
Add a shared history paragraph to planner_brief and critic_brief from the snapshot constants, with tests. Update the System facts mention of a plain copy only if it lives in this file.
Unreleased entry for the history file.
New decision: alternatives, choice, citation of job 20261024-115923-02gf, measured snapshot-time figure.

steps: Read crates/athena-git/src/lib.rs around Git::run_bytes and the log helpers; add a helper that runs `git log -n 2000 --first-parent -m --no-renames --name-only -z` with a custom format and parses it. Add a parser unit test.

In snapshot.rs add the constants and the PlainWithHistory variant. In `create`, return early for it after writing HISTORY.txt: classify all paths in one call, drop hidden paths and all-hidden commits, take the first 200, and write the text.
Write the snapshot tests: fixture with records/, private/ and mixed commits; a 205-commit cap case; no .git; user repo unchanged (status, HEAD, config).
In run.rs extract `planning_grant()`, switch both Snapshot::create calls (lines ~676 and ~815) to PlainWithHistory, and add the grant test.

In briefs.rs add the history paragraph to both briefs. athena-context may not depend on athena-git, so check Cargo.toml: if not, define constants in athena-context and have run.rs pass them, or add the constant to a shared crate. Add the brief tests and fix existing exact-text tests.
Measure snapshot time with and without history on this repository (several runs, median). Write the decisions.md entry with the measurement label, method and repo, and the CHANGELOG entry.
Run cargo fmt, clippy -D warnings and cargo test --locked, and fix failures.

risks.risk: athena-context may not depend on athena-git, so briefs cannot cite the constant directly.
risks.mitigation: Check the Cargo.toml dependency graph first. Otherwise put the constants in athena-context and have the snapshot code take them as a parameter, or re-export from a crate both depend on, with a test that equates them.

risks.risk: Commit subjects or paths could carry sensitive text from the history.
risks.mitigation: Only classified-visible paths are listed, and subjects of commits that touch visible paths are the same public history the repo already carries. Say so in the decision.

risks.risk: Git log on a very large history is slow.
risks.mitigation: The -n 2000 scan cap is measured and documented. The fixture-based time figure is recorded.

risks.risk: Exact-text tests of the briefs, or fake agents in the CLI tests, may break on the new paragraph or the new file.
risks.mitigation: Run the full cargo test and update the expectations. The fake planner ignores the snapshot contents.

risks.risk: A shallow clone or a repository with no first-parent history yields an empty log.
risks.mitigation: Write the file with a header and '(no commits)' rather than failing the snapshot.

demonstrations.method: Unit test in snapshot.rs. It builds a fixture repo with .gitattributes marking private/ athena-exclude, and commits touching src/, records/, private/, plus a mixed commit. A second test makes 205 commits. It creates a PlainWithHistory snapshot and reads HISTORY.txt.
demonstrations.observes: HISTORY.txt exists. It has one entry per visible commit with subject, date and paths. The records-only and private-only commits are absent. 'records/' and 'private' appear nowhere in the text. The mixed commit lists only its visible path. The 205-commit case has exactly 200 entries, the newest first.
demonstrations.fails_without: Without the history writer no HISTORY.txt exists. Without the classify filter the records/ or private text appears. Without the cap the 205-commit test counts 205.

demonstrations.method: Same test module. It snapshots the fixture and compares the user repo before and after.
demonstrations.observes: snapshot dir has no .git. `git status --porcelain`, HEAD, refs and .git/config of the user repo are the same before and after. Writing the history changed no tracked file.
demonstrations.fails_without: If the snapshot ran git init or copied .git, the .git-absence assertion fails.

demonstrations.method: Unit tests in briefs.rs on planner_brief and critic_brief built from existing test inputs.
demonstrations.observes: Each brief contains HISTORY_FILE's path, '200', 'subject', 'date', 'changed paths', 'records/', 'private', and 'Read' and 'Grep' in the history paragraph. The constant is used, not a literal. Existing brief tests that assert exact text are updated.
demonstrations.fails_without: Without the paragraph the brief has no mention of the file, so the assertions fail.

demonstrations.method: Test in run.rs on the new named function `planning_grant()`, which both the planner and critic call. It asserts the full value.
demonstrations.observes: tools are exactly Read, Grep and Glob; commands is empty (no Bash, no git); writes is false; permission_mode is dontAsk.
demonstrations.fails_without: If a git command or Bash were added, the equality assertion on commands/tools fails.

demonstrations.method: Measure by timing snapshot creation with and without the history on this repository, in a release or test build, over several runs. Record the median and spread, labelled as a measurement, with the repo, commit, and method, in docs/decisions.md. Use a temporary timing test or a one-off cargo run, not left in the tree.
demonstrations.observes: The decisions entry holds a figure in ms (plain copy vs plain copy plus history), the repo (this one), its commit count, and the run count. The figure is labelled measured.

demonstrations.method: Read the two files after the change.
demonstrations.observes: CHANGELOG Unreleased has an entry. The decisions entry lists the alternatives (repository in snapshot, widened git grants, plain copy), the choice, and cites job 20261024-115923-02gf.

demonstrations.method: Run the three checks. The boundary and personal-data policy tests in xtask run inside cargo test.
demonstrations.observes: All pass. Also run `cargo clippy --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings` and `cargo fmt --all --check` with clean output. The system_facts_budgets_match_computed test is unaffected because briefs sit outside the budget sets.
demonstrations.fails_without: A clippy or fmt violation, or a changed always-loaded prompt, would fail these.

open_questions: Whether athena-context can depend on athena-git (not checked); the constants' home depends on it.
The records-only versus all-hidden commit behavior follows the assumption in the reading (omit); the decision should state it.
Whether the 2000-commit scan cap is enough to find 200 visible commits in repositories where records/ commits dominate; the cap is a judgment, not measured.
